messages.body_plain:
Hi guys,

Thanks so much for all of this. What an amazing package!

Jessica - thank you for these scripts! I'm trying to do the same thing for loss only gambles. Did you ever figure it out? If not, I'll post them when I've figured it out.

Best,
Zoe

> Jessica

> > > > > > > Thanks,
> > > > > > > Jessica Mollick

messages.body_plain:
Hi Zoe and Young,

I had started making edits for losses, but I ran into some problems getting the model to converge. I was trying to model choosing between a risky loss or a sure loss. I'd be very interested in any scripts you come up with for a loss-only version, and the more flexible version of the toolbox when it's released.

I tried putting a negative sign in front of the cert option in the stan script to capture a sure loss, but I don't think that it worked.

evSafe     = - pow(cert[i,t], rho[i]);

This is what happens when I try and run my modified "loss only" version:
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'ra_noLA_edit_losses' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Rejecting initial value:
  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity.
  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value.

I've attached the scripts and text file I edited, in case they are helpful as you look into this further!

To run these in R, I just use the code snippet below:
library(hBayesDM)
output <- ra_noLA_edit_losses(data = "choose", niter = 2000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 3, ncore = 3)
plotInd(output, "rho")

Thanks,
Jessica

messages.subject: Re: Bounds
messages.body_plain:
Hi Graham,

Thanks for your kind words. All codes are available in our GitHub repo and you can check each model's Stan code to find out the bounds: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/tree/master/exec

Here is the link for the bandit2arm_delta mode where the upper bound of tau (inverse temperature) is set to 5 (line 25): https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/master/exec/bandit2arm_delta.stan. I set the upper bound to 5 because it's a reasonable value and posteriors rarely exceed the value. Let us know if the upper bound is causing a problem in your data.

We are updating our pipeline to make it easy to add/edit models. For now, to edit bounds of a parameter, you need to edit its Stan and R codes and rebuild the package.

Best,
Young
